Geologists use seismic imaging and other geophysical methods to better understand the geology and structure of Earth's crust by measuring and recording seismic waves generated by earthquakes, explosions or artificially created energy sources such as dynamite. These waves travel through the earth's interior and bounce back to the surface, where they are recorded by sensitive instruments called seismographs. By analyzing the speed, direction and intensity of these waves, geologists can study the composition, density, and structure of the rocks and other materials that make up the crust.

Seismic imaging involves using data from multiple seismographs to create detailed images of the subsurface structures. This technique is similar to a medical X-ray or CT scan, in which multiple images are taken to build a 3D image of the internal structures. Seismic imaging helps geologists to identify faults, folds, and other features in the crust that may indicate the presence of minerals, oil and gas deposits, or potential seismic hazards.

Other geophysical methods used by geologists include gravity surveys, magnetometry, and electrical resistivity surveys. Gravity surveys measure variations in the Earth's gravitational field to identify differences in the density of different rock types. Magnetometry measures the magnetic properties of the rocks to identify and map the location of mineral deposits. Electrical resistivity surveys use the natural electrical currents within the earth to measure the resistance of different rock types to electrical current, providing information on the composition and structure of the crust.

Overall, these geophysical methods provide valuable insights into the geology and structure of the Earth's crust, which is vital to understanding its history and potential for creating natural resources and hazards.

Equity financing is a way to raise capital by selling shares of ownership in a company. Equity financing does not require repayment of the funds borrowed, but the investors will receive a return on their investment through a dividend or the eventual sale of their shares.
